children: fell nearly 14% on Wednesday to record its worst single-day decline since May after a disappointing interim analysis from a Phase 2/3 trial for OCU410ST, its experimental therapy for a rare genetic eye disorder known as Stargardt disease.

In a regulatory filing on Wednesday, the company disclosed that the study’s independent Data Monitoring Committee has observed a negative treatment effect in the interim sample comprising 26 trial subjects.

While the analysis focused on atrophic lesion size in those who completed their eight-month clinical assessments, the DMC recommended the trial continue until eight months of follow-up data for the entire study population are available.

“The DMC noted that one could consider futility based on the negative direction of treatment effect on the interim sample and other interim results, but the DMC recommended the modification to obtain the entire dataset at 8 months,” Ocugen
The company said it intends to heed the DMC recommendation and analyze the entire eight-month follow-up data from the study. With its Q2 2026 results last month, Ocugen
